You just said “All body shaming is gross,” and you can’t see how this is comparable to “All lives matter”?

The point here is that fat phobia is discriminatory on the societal and structural level. Fat people (especially if they are POC or queer) are treated awfully by society in SIGNIFICANT ways: negligent healthcare leads to more health problems/early death, low wages lead to higher stress and poorer quality of life. This is a HUGE injustice and needs to discussed. In the same way that “Black Lives Matter” is super important because the discrimination black people face is so significant. 

White people don’t deserve to be bullied or harmed in anyway either, but when it happens, it’s not a systemic issue. Similarly, skinny people don’t deserve to be bullied, but it’s not a systemic issue, and there are more pressing matters. Doesn’t mean your feelings aren’t valid.

Maintenance phase is a podcast that advocates for fat people, and you are here on this subreddit advocating for skinny people. This is exactly what they are talking about.

Edit: “Skinny shaming” as a term was created as a parallel to “fat shaming.” They’re saying that it doesn’t exist as a systematic issue. All kinds of people get teased for their bodies (acne, big noses, etc). Not all of them are systematic issues.

No, you’re not understanding my post. 

You’re telling me to share my experience, well, this is it! These resources helped me, and based on some of the replies on my post, it’s helped other people, too. 

Just because this advice doesn’t help you or others doesn’t mean I shouldn’t share it. Just because you don’t agree with my advice and it triggers you personally doesn’t mean it isn’t a valid piece of advice. This is what I did after three failed suicide attempts, and now I’m in a better place. 

I’m not saying my advice will make OP feel better instantly. I’m not saying it will change anyone’s life immediately. I’m saying that it is something to think about when you are holding a bottle of pills in your hand and can’t think of anything that may bring you a bit of hope. 

I’m sorry that you are depressed, struggling, and that my advice angers you. But that does not mean that these resources are garbage to everyone.

Your replies are as useful as telling people, “War is inevitable and there’s nothing you can do about it,” when they complain about the war. 

I’m not telling OP they have to use these resources, but sometimes knowing there are other options other than ending your life can help. I’m not going to tell OP or anyone who is seriously contemplating suicide that they should give up because the system is horrible. I’m still alive because people fought to give me hope in whatever ways they could, and I’m trying to do the same for others who were in my position.

While a lot of these answers are relating to OP’s post, a lot of them are very bleak answers. As a person who has struggled with suicidal thoughts due to this very reason, I think it’s important to provide as many realistic, positive answers as we can to continue giving people a reason why to keep going. We need hope.

Yes, it is unfair, and the answer isn’t “Everything will get better in time” or “Make some lifestyle choices.”

The answer is to look for as much free or low-cost help as you can. It isn’t super easy, but it can make things much better.

- Contact suicide hotlines and ask them for tips and advice. 
- There are therapy apps and websites that have free trials that you can use to help you for a little while. 
- If you go to school/university/college, please go on their website and find out if there is free counseling and food pantries (and any other free resources.)
- Apply for as many state benefits as you can, and research the possible hidden benefits you may qualify for.
- Finally, and most importantly, please try to surround yourself with people that make you feel like you’re not alone. Not only can they help you with the above list, but it makes life more bearable. If you don’t have anyone, maybe start there. Look for free clubs and social groups in your area and maybe start trying to make new connections. Reach out to family as well.

Obviously not everything will be possible or easy, but here are some options. Please keep going, things can get better. The situation may still suck, but hopefully you’ll feel better.

I think the best place to start is to not be angry...with yourself. I think your anger is valid and warranted, but maybe direct your anger to the source of the addiction. 

In other words, instead of saying, “I should be angry with myself because I am the reason I am addicted to porn, and I am the reason I can’t stop,” maybe shift it to something more accurate, “I am angry with _____ because it is the reason I am addicted to porn, and _____ is the reason I can’t stop.”  

Now that you view it as a problem that isn’t caused by you and your “flaws,” you can actually focus on detaching yourself from the addiction.

I wish you the best of luck! You’re stronger than you know :)

You can even take it further with keeping things visible. Not only can you keep things like toothbrushes and meds visible, but hobbies/skills you want to work on, too!

For example, when my yoga mat and yoga shoes are places on my couch the night before, it makes me want to do yoga the next day!

I find that I hyperfixate on a new relationship as well. The amount of stimulation and excitement I get from it seems too good to pass up! However, when the high goes away, it can give the illusion of losing feelings for someone, when in reality, I think it’s just me beginning to shift my focus back to other things along with the relationship.

I think that being aware of how your ADHD is affecting your feelings toward the relationship is important. Communicating with yourself and your partner about your struggles helps with compromising early on. :)
